📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-04-crm-amqp-consumer-monitor-family-quiet-period-flap`
This is occurrence #20 in the last 7 days (139 all-time). (DD-scan-diff synthetic — no Slack MCP this session.)
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `CRM Experience` (`@customer-management` / `#team-customer-management`)
Playbook: 1) Confirm shape: monitor ID is one of the 5 sibling AMQP-consumer monitors, name matches '[CRM] <service> throughput dropped (possible stall)' or '[CRM] <service> heartbeat — consumer silent'. 2) Pull `scripts/dd_search.py metric --query 'sum:trace.amqp.command.hits{service:<name>,env:prod}.as_rate()'` over a multi-hour window — expect a genuine but brief dip below the monitor's floor, not a data gap/tool failure. 3) Confirm `service:<name> status:error` in DD Logs returns 0 for the window. 4) Check sibling outbound-5xx/P95-latency monitors for the same service — if also OK throughout, this is the benign quiet-period pattern. 5) Escalate only if unresolved after ~1h or a sibling error/latency monitor co-fires. 6) Do not re-investigate from scratch on each recurrence.
Open Jira: n/a — no fix_jira on this entry (fix_status: monitoring-noise-suspected-unconfirmed)

Source alerts (1 total, DD-scan-diff synthetic — no Slack MCP this session):
  • monitor 302055141, last_triggered 2026-08-19T08:03:21Z (OK, recovered by scan time)

Root-cause analysis:
  • Query: `dd_search.py metric --query 'sum:trace.amqp.command.hits{service:method-mobile-notifications-subscriber,env:prod}.as_rate()'`, window 2026-08-19T06:00:00Z–09:00:00Z
  • Observed: genuine ~76-minute data gap 06:44Z→08:00Z (consumer effectively silent), throughput resumes to 0.03–0.23 msg/s by 08:00–08:59Z; overall_state_modified 08:03:21Z is 3 min after traffic resumed; 0 hits on `service:method-mobile-notifications-subscriber status:error` for the full window
  • Reasoning: matches the documented benign quiet-period trip-then-recover shape — no corroborating error, consistent with the 5-sibling-monitor family's chronic pattern

Evidence:
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/302055141 (state: OK, recovered)
  • DD metric: https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.amqp.command.hits&exp_scope=service%3Amethod-mobile-notifications-subscriber%2Cenv%3Aprod&exp_agg=avg&start=1755583200&end=1755593400
  • DD logs (0-hit error check): https://app.datadoghq.com/logs?query=service%3Amethod-mobile-notifications-subscriber%20status%3Aerror&from_ts=1755583200000&to_ts=1755593400000&live=false
  • This-window concentration: n/a — single-service AMQP-consumer monitor, no per-service ES breakdown applicable (evidence_source: datadog_apm)

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-07-notifications-p95-latency-monitor-noise`
This is occurrence #37 (cumulative total; degraded-mode DD-scan-diff cycle, no Slack MCP this session). last_notified_at was 2026-08-16T11:25:00Z — ~72h51m ago, 24h suppression window had expired.
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `CRM Experience` (`@customer-management` / `#team-customer-management`)
Playbook: 1) Confirm shape: re-query p95:trace.aspnet.request{service:notifications,env:prod} over the monitor's own last_10m window plus a wider surrounding window — expect values in the 0.001-0.2s range, nowhere near 1s. 2) Check 0 error logs on service:notifications for the window. 3) Do not treat as user-impacting — cleanest non-reproduction pattern in the monitor-noise family. 4) If a genuinely elevated p95 is ever seen, treat as a break from this pattern and escalate immediately.
Open Jira: n/a — no fix_jira on this entry (fix_status: monitoring-noise-suspected-unconfirmed)

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-03-eda-consumer-amqp-stopped-publishing`
This is occurrence #7 in the last 7 days (55 all-time). (DD-scan-diff synthetic — no Slack MCP this session.)
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Integrations` (`@connect` / `#team-connect` — ownership.md's "EDA-stack" project row maps to team Integrations; DD monitor tag says `team:devops`, ownership.md is authoritative per step 4.1a)
Playbook: 1) Confirm shape: DD monitor 296641466 in 'No Data' state. 2) ALWAYS check the sibling P1 monitors first — 296632224 (Event ingest stopped) and 296636101 (Kafka events stopped) — if both are OK, the core EDA pipeline is healthy and this is very unlikely to be user-impacting. 3) Confirm service:eda_consumer status:error in DD Logs returns 0. 4) If sibling monitors are also firing, escalate immediately. 5) Do not treat as actionable on a single occurrence.
Open Jira: n/a — no fix_jira on this entry (fix_status: escalated-for-review)

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-06-runtime-core-redis-cache-timeout-transient-burst`
This is occurrence #1 in the last 7 days (22 all-time). (DD-scan-diff synthetic — no Slack MCP this session.)
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Vertical App Experience` (`@sales management` / `#team-sales-management` — per ownership.md, `runtime-core-api` → Vertical App Experience)
Playbook: 1) Confirm shape: monitor 227940275 in Alert (or recently Alert, now OK/self-recovered) with last_triggered_ts within the last ~15 min, and NOT co-firing with RTC p95 (115456700/117279738), tables-fields Redis circuit-breaker (302103451), or gateway XHR (77419271) -- if any of those ARE co-firing, treat as the shared-upstream-slowness pattern documented under ki-2026-05-24/ki-2026-07-06-tables-fields-redis-circuitbreaker instead. 2) Query trace.redis.command.errors by {service} for the +/-10min window to confirm which service(s) took the hit. 3) ES search messageTemplate.keyword:"Redis operation timed out after 5 seconds" AND fields.dd_service.keyword:runtime-core-api in a tight window to corroborate genuine cache-client impact; count distinct fields.Account.AccountName.keyword to gauge blast radius. 4) Check deploy correlation on runtime-core if the repo is fetchable that cycle. 5) If this recurs with the same standalone/no-deploy shape, this is chronic infra noise -- bump occurrences, no further escalation needed.
Open Jira: n/a — no fix_jira on this entry (fix_status: chronic-residual, needs-human default)

Source alerts (1 total, DD-scan-diff synthetic — no Slack MCP this session):
  • monitor 227940275, last_triggered 2026-08-19T13:30:35+00:00 (OK, self-recovered by scan time)

Root-cause analysis:
  • Query: `dd_search.py metric --query "sum:trace.redis.command.errors{env:prod} by {service}.as_count()"`, window 2026-08-19T13:20:35Z–13:40:35Z
  • Observed: single series `service:runtime-core-api`, 105 + 44 = 149 errors, both points at 13:23:40–13:23:50Z (~10s burst, self-recovered ~7min before the monitor's own eval); RTC p95 and tables-fields circuit-breaker monitors last fired 2026-08-16 or earlier — not co-firing
  • Reasoning: fresh by-service breakdown confirms this is the standalone runtime-core-api mechanism (this KB family covers 3 distinct services behind the same monitor) — matches all 21 prior occurrences of this specific entry, not the tables-fields or nonprod/apps siblings

Evidence:
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/227940275 (state: OK, recovered)
  • DD metric: https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.redis.command.errors&exp_scope=service%3Aruntime-core-api&exp_agg=sum&start=1787145635&end=1787146835
